scope: Proposition 9.6 (Backward escape and flow bounds) of the manuscript “Quantitative Near-Kerr Evolution and Generic C2 Future Inextendibility” (preprints/Quantitative-Near-Kerr-Evolution-and-Generic-C2-Future-Inextendibility-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 264 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cd38cc55e3c203a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 103. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The null rays launched by dv on a sufficiently small fixed entry patch, followed towards the past, return to the original initial end. For every prescribed α > 0, after choosing a sufficiently large fixed radius and then taking T sufficiently large, all their arrival points satisfy (1 − α)tT < |z − z∗| < (1 + α)tT , z∗ = Ce(tT ). (E1) Their entry crossing is unique and transverse within the computing region, with separation from the entry level outside a uniform collar. All fixed jets of the phase-space flow on all subsegments, including launch-center derivatives, have bounds eo(T). Tensor parallel transport has bounded norm and inverse along these rays. The assertions hold with short past and future launch margins, including passage through the deeper inner exit.
